react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on two interconnected metabolic themes: one-carbon/folate biochemistry and membrane lipid remodelling. In the RaMP multi-DB ORA, Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260) is the overwhelming winner at FDR = 3.1 × 10⁻¹⁶ with 7 of the 11 input metabolites hitting a 57-member pathway (fold enrichment 664). This top hit is independently reproduced by mummichog's m/z-direct network as 'Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism' (MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism, p = 0.023, 8/8 metabolites) and is supported by MetaboAnalystR PSEA on KEGG (hsa00260, nominal p = 1.0 after FDR but shared membership). The WikiPathways pathway 'Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways' (WP:WP2525) achieves rank 8 in RaMP (FDR = 8.8 × 10⁻¹⁴, 6/60 metabolites), directly linking the one-carbon cycle to the trans-sulfuration branch through shared driver metabolites S-adenosylmethionine and L-cystathionine. MetaboAnalystR independently detects the cysteine/methionine axis as KEGG hsa00270 (p = 9 × 10⁻⁴), the single most significant single-DB result across the KEGG library. A second cross-paradigm axis emerges around glycerophospholipid metabolism: RaMP's generic 'Biochemical pathways: part I' (WP:WP3604, rank 9, FDR = 3.3 × 10⁻¹³) and mummichog both capture the Choline → Phosphorylcholine node (KEGG hsa00564 / MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism, p = 0.045). Biocytin (vitamin H/biotin metabolism) and Uridine 5'-monophosphate (pyrimidine metabolism) appear only in single-tool contexts. The dominant driver constellation spans: phosphoserine (choline/biocytin upstream), choline and phosphorylcholine (membrane lipid), S-adenosylmethionine (methyl donor), L-cystathionine (trans-sulfuration junction), and AMP (energy/adenine). Cholesterol, while present, scores only in low-rank or peripheral contexts. The biological story is a treatment-induced reconfiguration of the serine–glycine–one-carbon network with secondary perturbation of phosphatidylcholine homeostasis, consistent with altered methyl-group metabolism and oxidative-stress defence capacity.

Biocytin and uridine 5′-monophosphate appear only in peripheral, non-significant contexts. RaMP multi-DB ORA returns KEGG:map00260 "Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism" as its top result (rank 0, FDR = 3.1 × 10⁻¹⁶), hitting 7 of 11 input metabolites. The same ORA hits WP:WP2525 "Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways" at rank 8 (FDR = 8.8 × 10⁻¹⁴) with 6 hits, capturing SAM and L-cystathionine that link the folate one-carbon cycle to the trans-sulfuration branch. Mummichog, operating on m/z signatures in the metabolic-function network, independently recovers "Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism" as its top hit (p = 0.018) with 8 of 8 input compounds resolved, and ranks "Glycerophospholipid metabolism" second (p = 0.044), capturing choline, phosphorylcholine, and cholesterol as membrane-remodelling signals.   "narrative_text": "Two complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism as the dominant signal in the differentially abundant metabolite set. react_result.final_narrative_text: Two complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism as the dominant signal in the differentially abundant metabolite set. RaMP multi-database ORA reports KEGG:map00260 (Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism) at rank 0 with FDR = 3.11 × 10⁻¹⁶ and fold enrichment = 664; seven of the eleven input compounds hit this pathway. Mummichog m/z-direct activity analysis on the metabolic-function network independently recovers the equivalent functional module, ranking MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine metabolism first (p = 0.010) with all eight resolved input compounds captured and no annotation gaps. The six shared compounds across both analyses are O-phospho-L-serine, choline, sarcosine, AMP, S-adenosyl-L-methionine, and L-cystathionine, with (R)-lipoic acid confirmed only by RaMP. Phosphocholine additionally co-locates with cholesterol in the secondary hit MUMM:glycerophospholipid metabolism (rank 1, p = 0.031), implicating membrane phospholipid remodeling as a secondary biological theme. The primary driver compound is O-phospho-L-serine (KEGG:C01005), which feeds into the serine-to-glycine branch via PHGDH (EC 1.1.1.95). The choline-to-phosphocholine conversion is catalyzed by choline kinase (CHKB; EC 2.7.1.32), linking the membrane lipid signal to the one-carbon/trans-sulfuration axis. L-Cystathionine (KEGG:C02291) is a pathway member confirmed by both RaMP and Mummichog, consistent with trans-sulfuration wiring. UMP (KEGG:C00105) and biocytin (KEGG:C05552) remain peripheral to the primary amino-acid pool and do not achieve significance in either paradigm.

The six shared compounds across both analyses are O-phospho-L-serine, choline, sarcosine, AMP, S-adenosyl-L-methionine, and L-cystathionine, with (R)-lipoic acid confirmed only by RaMP. Phosphocholine additionally co-locates with cholesterol in the secondary hit MUMM:glycerophospholipid metabolism (rank 1, p = 0.031), implicating membrane phospholipid remodeling as a secondary biological theme. The primary driver compound is O-phospho-L-serine (KEGG:C01005), which feeds into the serine-to-glycine branch via PHGDH (EC 1.1.1.95). The choline-to-phosphocholine conversion is catalyzed by choline kinase (CHKB; EC 2.7.1.32), linking the membrane lipid signal to the one-carbon/trans-sulfuration axis. L-Cystathionine (KEGG:C02291) is a pathway member confirmed by both RaMP and Mummichog, consistent with trans-sulfuration wiring. UMP (KEGG:C00105) and biocytin (KEGG:C05552) remain peripheral to the primary amino-acid pool and do not achieve significance in either paradigm.
